topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the cancer lecture series, and the key learning outcomes regarding environmental exposures and mechanisms of carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Intrinsic and environmental determinants of cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the fundamental nature of cancer development, evaluating the relative contributions of intrinsic genetic errors, environmental exposures, and lifestyle factors supported by population epidemiological data.

topics.label: Infectious agents in oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how pathogens drive malignancy, using the multi-step pathogenesis of Burkitt lymphoma involving Epstein-Barr virus and malaria as a detailed case study.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and metabolic activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the molecular mechanisms by which chemical and physical agents induce DNA damage, focusing on how host xenobiotic metabolism converts inert compounds into reactive carcinogens.

topics.label: Cancer initiation, promotion, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how non-mutagenic promoters, chronic inflammation, and host developmental stages cooperate with mutational initiation to drive tumor outgrowth.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and evaluating carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo animal, and in vitro experimental approaches utilized to detect carcinogen exposure and measure carcinogenic potential.

topics.label: Closing remarks on carcinogen risk and benefit
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the lecture's conclusion by summarising the challenges of determining carcinogenicity and framing exposure in terms of everyday risk-benefit decisions.
